objective: Integrate a reviewable dual-motor traction architecture, independent power childboard, and mechanical envelopes without representing unknown motor, regeneration, thermal, safety, supplier, or physical evidence as complete.
acceptance: the system architecture distinguishes the two chassis traction motors from the six vendor-controlled UR5e joints
the traction childboard is independently replaceable and its controlled motor-power input does not assume the isolated converter can absorb regenerative energy
the childboard interface preserves the hardwired MOTOR_ENABLE_SAFE path and cannot treat a software request as a safety output
motor, driver, MOSFET, fuse, bulk capacitance, clamp, shunt, connector, and thermal selections remain fail-closed until approved ratings and evidence exist
motor voltage selection, regeneration, and bus overshoot are explicit release blockers for either the 12 V auxiliary baseline or a protected 48 V traction-bus alternative
connector pinout tables agree with the detailed controller schematic and generator
the childboard power and return topology explicitly closes VM_PROTECTED, VCC_LOGIC, GND_MOTOR, GND_LOGIC and the isolated CAN island with one STAR_GND_01 join
U1 nFAULT reaches two independent hardware safety-gate inhibit paths with default-low fail-closed behavior and no software dependency

the controlled harness package covers H02 J_PWR plus J_SAFE, J_CAN, J_ML, J_MR, J_ENC_L and J_ENC_R; H11-H14 terminate at external M1/M2 motor and encoder endpoints with explicit pin maps and active/shield/drain semantics while retaining MPN and physical-test holds
J_SAFE is explicitly a future controller J10/K1/K2 safety ECO endpoint and is not wired to or substituted by the current single-channel J11
all fourteen controlled harness rows are validated for endpoint identity, pin-map syntax, conductor-count reconciliation and shield/drain semantics
the placement contract fixes J_SAFE, J_CAN, J_ML and J_MR on the +Y_REAR edge and checks declared motor-harness bend radii
the harness report cross-checks the candidate 11 A dual-stall demand against the controller J2 10 A aggregate ceiling and keeps the mismatch release-blocking
mechanical artifacts include left and right motor envelopes plus a serviceable childboard envelope
deterministic validators and hardware tests cover the new engineering package
no supplier DFM, safety approval, firmware behavior, or physical bring-up evidence is inferred
evidence: hardware/motor_driver/kicad traction-childboard design artifacts if generated
stop_conditions: an actual motor MPN or motor electrical envelope would have to be invented
a 60 V bus transient or regenerative energy path lacks an approved clamp and absorption design
the safety path could energize traction from software alone
the candidate power/ground return or nFAULT fan-out is not explicitly closed in the controlled topology tables
KiCad DRC, ERC, connectivity, or deterministic package validation fails
supplier DFM, approved AVL, calibrated physical measurements, or safety certification is required
